name: Table
description: Native `<table>` semantics with the kit's chrome: render real table/thead/tbody/tr/th/td elements (useRender passthrough), so `scope`, screen-reader navigation and keyboard behaviour stay intact. A caller that wants a visually header-less table keeps its `<TableHead>` and hides it with `sr-only`; omitting the header would drop the semantics.

name: TableScroll
description: The area a table wider than its container scrolls sideways in (table.md, "Wide tables"): a horizontal ScrollArea around a `Table` or a plain `<table>`, so the table scrolls and the page doesn't. It only overflows sideways, so it never holds back the page's vertical scroll, and it is a tab stop while the table is wider than it, so the keyboard can scroll it. It has no frame of its own: `className` sizes and frames it, and `ref`, `onScroll` and the native props go to the element that scrolls.

props.name: actionsRef
props.type: ((instance: ScrollAreaActions | null) => void | (() => void | { [UNDEFINED_VOID_ONLY]: never; }) | DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES[keyof DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES]) | RefObject<ScrollAreaActions | null>
props.description: Methods to scroll from code that the container doesn't have natively.

props.name: children
props.description: The scrolling content, in ScrollArea's own container.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Class of a content element around `children`, inside the container: put padding and the content's own layout (grid, flex, `gap`, `stack-y-*`) here, so the scrollbars stay at the edges and the gutters layer is never one of the laid-out children. Only with it, `contentStyle` or `fade` is there one.

props.name: contentRef
props.description: An element whose size is the content's, watched for size changes (such as a hidden mirror of a textarea's text). Without it each element child of the container is watched, and children added or removed.

props.name: contentStyle
props.description: Style of the content element; renders it, as `contentClassName` does.

props.name: fade
props.description: Fade the content out toward an edge that has more past it. The scrollbars don't fade.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: How long the scrollbars stay after scrolling stops, in ms. At least 100 with `trigger="scroll"`.

props.name: onEdgeChange
props.description: Called when the area reaches or leaves an edge, and after mounting when the content overflows.

props.name: onScroll
props.description: The container's scroll events.

props.name: overscroll
props.description: What a scroll that reaches the end does: stop there with no bounce (`none`, the default), stop there but let Mac trackpads and iOS bounce the area (`contain`), or carry on to the page behind (`auto`, which leaves the container's own `overscroll-behavior` alone). Only in the directions the area overflows right now.

props.name: railInset
props.description: Room in px the scrollbars keep clear at each end, such as a sticky header's height, so they don't run over it. Also settable in CSS, on the root: `--r-scroll-area-rail-inset-{top,bottom,left,right}`, which don't inherit.

props.name: render
props.description: Another element in place of ScrollArea's own `<div>`, as the container (an element or a function that gets the props). It must hold children: the gutters are its first child.

props.name: size
props.description: Thumb thickness: `small` is 5px, `medium` 7px; both grow while pointed at or dragged.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description: The container's: by default `0` while there is something to scroll.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the scrollbars show. They always show while scrolling or dragging.

name: TableSortableHead
description: A column heading that sorts the rows (table.md, "Sorting"): a `TableHead` whose label is a `TableSortButton` filling the cell, with `aria-sort` on the cell and a 12px arrow on the sorted column only. Which column is sorted is the caller's: pass `sort` and update it from `onSortChange`. With `render={<div role="columnheader" />}` it draws a th-like cell, with the header type, line and padding, and sets no `scope`, which only a `th` takes. Native props, `className` and the ref go to the heading cell, not the button.

props.name: align
props.description: `"right"` for a right-aligned column, such as numbers: the label ends on the column's right edge and the arrow goes before it. Pass the same value to the column's cells.

props.name: firstSort
props.description: The direction of a first click, when the rows aren't sorted by this column: `"descending"` for numbers and dates, `"ascending"` for text.

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: Called with the next direction: the reverse of `sort`, or `firstSort`.

props.name: sort
props.description: The column's current sort, or undefined when the rows aren't sorted by it. Sets `aria-sort` on the heading cell and draws the arrow.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

name: TableSortButton
description: The button of a heading that sorts, on its own, for a header row drawn without `Table` (table.md, "Sorting"): the label, the 12px arrow on the sorted column (its room kept, empty, on the others), the label's color, the touch hit area and the sort cycle. It fills the heading cell around it, so the whole cell is the target. It has no padding and no border and inherits the font: the cell sets the type, height and line and has no padding, and the row's horizontal padding goes on the button through `className`. Set `aria-sort` on that cell, which needs `role="columnheader"` inside a `role="row"` in a `role="table"` or `role="grid"`; in development a warning says when there is no such cell or its `aria-sort` isn't `sort`. Native props, `className` and the ref go to the button.

props.name: align
props.description: `"right"` for a right-aligned column, such as numbers: the label ends on the column's right edge and the arrow goes before it.

props.name: firstSort
props.description: The direction of a first click, when the rows aren't sorted by this column: `"descending"` for numbers and dates, `"ascending"` for text.

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: Called with the next direction: the reverse of `sort`, or `firstSort`.

props.name: sort
props.description: The column's current sort, or undefined when the rows aren't sorted by it. Draws the arrow and colors the label; set the same value as `aria-sort` on the heading cell around the button (in development, a warning says when they differ).
